entries.note: Draws the dieline into an element; shows a hint when the type has no spec or the size is incomplete.
Returns the SVG text only.
Returns the flat (unfolded) width and height.

name: Dieline Engine (TMDieline)
purpose: Draws the flat dieline of a product type from its dimensions, live while Sales types the size.
inputs: The dieline recipe of the product type (prod_type.dieline_spec): canvas size, variables and a list of elements (cut, crease, bleed, hole) written as formulas.
The sizes typed on the form: product length (A), width (B), height (C), diameter, lid height, glue flap, tuck flaps, dust flap, overflow margin.
outputs: Cut lines red, crease lines green, bleed grey dashed, holes blue.
Width and height of the unfolded sheet, used by Pro-Dev as the starting size for imposition.
steps: Reads the short names (A, B, C, ...) and maps them to the form fields.
Evaluates every formula of the recipe with those values (plus, minus, times, divide, max, min, round ...). No geometry is hard coded.
Computes the canvas width and height; without a valid size nothing is drawn.
Draws each element of the recipe in order and returns one SVG.

entries.note: One plano, one flat size: the basic layout.
Level 1: tries every flap length in the allowed range and ranks the results.
Level 2: also tries the "69" interlock, the second copy turned 180 degrees and shifted.
Tool #2: tries all active standard planos and ranks them by paper used.
Tool #10: two parts of one product on the same sheet, compared with separate sheets.
Tool #4: running metres of cutting and creasing rule for the die.
Position of every piece on the sheet (mm), for the drawing.
Flat size = body plus flap on the chosen side.

name: Imposition Engine
purpose: Finds how many pieces (UP) fit on a plano sheet and which layout wastes the least paper.
inputs: Flat (unfolded) size of one piece in mm.
Strip the press needs to grip the sheet, in mm.
Free edge around the sheet in mm.
Allowed flap length range and the side the flap sits on (sweep tools).
Order quantity; when given, the best sheet is judged on the sheets really needed for it.
outputs: TEGAK (upright), PUTAR (rotated) or CAMPUR (main block plus a rotated block in the rest area).
Share of the usable area that is used / wasted.
Columns, rows and piece size per block: the data behind the drawing.
Usable area after margin and gripper.
combinePair only: COMBINED, SEPARATE or NONE, and the area saved per set.
steps: Usable area = plano minus margins and gripper.
Counts pieces upright and rotated; the higher count wins.
Tries the mixed layout: upright block first, then rotated pieces in the remaining strip; kept only when it gives more pieces.
Efficiency = area of all pieces divided by the usable area.
The sweep tools repeat this for every flap length (and shift), then rank by UP, then by efficiency.
The officer picks one of the top results. Nothing is saved by the engine.
writes: Nothing: pure calculation. The Pro-Dev screen saves the chosen layout to prod_layout_group.

entries.note: Calculates the three sections. Writes nothing.
Saves the result to the part; sections the officer overrode or typed by hand are left alone.
BOP and BOM for one Work Order quantity, from the layout Pro-Dev already saved.
Rows on the part that do not come from the engine (override / manual).

name: Spec Engine (BOP · BOM · Ink)
purpose: Builds the production specification of a part: process steps, materials and ink configuration.
inputs: The inquiry part: finishing, material, colour notation, quantity per pack, order quantity, artwork.
Layout decisions of Pro-Dev: sheet size, plano size, sheets per plano, press, die-cut machine, UP, order quantity, artwork colours.
Sections the officer changed (bop, bom, inks); null = follow the engine.
outputs: Bill of Process: steps in order with the suggested machine.
Bill of Material: material, quantity, unit, waste.
What is missing or unusual (no machine fits, no rule for a finishing ...).
The officer sections, normalised, ready to save.
steps: Reads the inquiry input and the layout decisions.
Applies the admin rules in prod_bop_rule to turn finishing and material into process steps and usage rates.
Calculates sheets, material quantities and ink per colour for the order quantity.
Returns the result with a source per row: ENGINE, OVERRIDE (officer changed it) or MANUAL (old / typed data).
On Save, only ENGINE sections are rewritten; "back to the engine result" removes an override.

entries.note: Runs monthly (prodev:usage-rates) or on demand.

name: Usage Rate Engine
purpose: Learns material usage rates and waste percentages from real production data and proposes new values for the BOP rules.
inputs: Start date of the production data to learn from.
true = write the proposals; false = only show them.
outputs: Per rule: current rate, proposed rate, sample size.
How many rules were changed automatically (only rules marked auto apply).
Size of the sample, the period and a remark when there is too little data.
steps: Proposed rate = current rate x (material really used / material planned).
Planned = quantity required on the Work Order; real = issued from the warehouse minus returned.
Waste per process = defect / (good + defect) from the production output records.
Below the minimum sample nothing is proposed.
Values typed by an officer are never overwritten; a rule is changed without asking only when it is marked auto apply.
writes: tm2mst.prod_bop_rule (proposal columns; the rate itself only with auto apply)

name: Routing Template Engine
purpose: Checks the order of process steps and turns a routing template into ready steps with a suggested machine.
inputs: Steps to check: process, sequence, branch. May be an unsaved draft.
The routing template to check or to apply.
Sheet length, sheet width, gsm: machines that cannot take the size are not suggested.
The product, to find the templates that fit it.
outputs: Order that is technically impossible (stripping before die-cutting).
Unusual order that still has real cases; never stops the officer.
Each step with the suggested machine and its resolved parameters.
Templates that fit the product; the default first, never chosen silently when there is no default.
steps: Compares each pair of steps with the precedence table.
For each step, picks a machine from the process x machine capability matrix that fits the sheet size and gsm.
Parameters come from three layers: the process x machine pair, then the machine, then the process default.

name: Costing Engine (Pro-Cost)
purpose: Calculates the cost price (HPP) of every part and the selling price per quantity tier of an inquiry.
restricted: The cost recipe is confidential (Costing and Directors only). This page shows the flow, not the formulas or rates.
inputs: The costing document (iqp_costing) with its parts, coatings and price tiers.
DC, DC+SF, DC+SHEET, KRAFT (offset family) or SHEET, SHEET_DIGITAL (corrugated).
Paper and grammage, print size, plano size, UP, coating, lamination, tooling, quantity per set, tolerance.
Quantity, tolerance, margin (non VAT and VAT), rounding step and mode.
Mode 1: pulled from the confirmed Pro-Dev layout. Mode 2: typed by the officer. Both must give the same HPP for the same geometry.
outputs: Paper, sheet, process, coating, lamination and tooling cost per piece, and the part total.
Total material, process and finishing cost per piece, and tooling for the order.
HPP per piece, price after tolerance, after rounding, after margin, and the price with VAT.
steps: Takes the main tier quantity as the base quantity.
Calculates every part with the rule of its type (offset family or corrugated).
Rolls the parts up to the header, weighted by quantity per set.
For every tier: adds tooling divided by that quantity, applies tolerance (rule differs per part type), rounding, margin and VAT.
Everything runs in one transaction; rates are frozen on the document, so later master changes do not move an old costing.

entries.note: Fills only empty boxes: Inquiry BOM, Pro-Dev waste, part template rates, Costing constants, masters; history replaces the default when enough similar costings exist.
Remembers that the officer changed a box (override) or deliberately set it to 0 (never restored).
A box that had a suggestion and was blanked by accident gets its suggested value back.
Called by Calculate: stores the final value of every box with its context (part type, quantity) as learning data.
Calculation Report: price steps, comparison with similar costings, notes, source of the boxes, quick simulations.
Core boxes that are still empty and need a look before the price is trusted.

name: Costing Advisor (fills the boxes, explains the price, learns)
purpose: Fills the empty Pro-Cost boxes in the background, explains the result in a Calculation Report, and learns from what the officer finally uses.
restricted: Margin and cost are confidential (Costing and Directors only). The report is shown only to logins allowed to see the formula.
inputs: The costing document with parts and price tiers (Mode 1 pulled from Inquiry and Pro-Dev, Mode 2 typed by the officer).
iqp_costing_recommendation rows learned from earlier Calculate clicks, same part type.
outputs: Written to iqp_costing_part and iqp_costing_price_tier, only where the box was empty.
One row per box: suggested value, source, sample count, override and zero-intent flags.
Array shown in five accordion sections under the price card.
steps: Default 18% margin (constant MARGIN_DEFAULT_PCT); below 5 similar costings (ADVISOR_MIN_SAMPLE_STAT) the default or derived value is used.
From 5 similar costings: median of the officer final values. From 30 (ADVISOR_MIN_SAMPLE_ML): light nearest-neighbour model by quantity, used only if it beats the median in leave-one-out.

Part template rates (prod_part_template, imported from tmhpp) fill rates only, never the product geometry. The template also gives the paper kind and gsm when the Inquiry BOM is empty; the nearest ACTIVE grammage (tmhpp prices) is used.

No Pro-Dev layout yet: the Imposition Engine is run read-only over all active plano sizes and the cheapest layout per piece fills plano, UP and print size (marked as estimate, replaced by the real layout later).
Tolerance default = constant TOLERANCE_DEFAULT_PCT (median of nine old tmhpp documents) until enough history exists.
The report repeats the CostingEngine tier formula for explanation and checks it equals the stored price; if not, the step list is hidden.

name: Reverse Costing
purpose: Turns a stand-alone (instant) costing into an integrated one by creating the documents that normally come before it.
inputs: An instant costing that has no inquiry yet.
outputs: A new inquiry of type NEW linked to the costing.
Created as Draft; only a person can Confirm it.
steps: Creates the Master Product and its parts (Draft).
Creates the inquiry and its parts and links them to the costing.
Creates the Pro-Dev layout as Draft.
The numbers of the costing do not change: the parts stay "typed by officer".

entries.note: Sends the document to the first step that matches; null = no active flow, the document stays where it is.
Approves the waiting step and opens the next one, or ends the flow.
Stops the flow; a reason is required.
Postpones the decision; the status does not change.
The approval queue of one user, including positions he is acting for.

name: Flow Engine (Approval)
purpose: Moves a document through its approval steps, the same way for every module.
inputs: Which flow: CO, PR, PO, AD ...
Status the document leaves (for example DRAFT).
Document value; steps can apply to a range of amounts.
Division, when the flow differs per division.
The step being decided and the reason (reject / hold).
outputs: The step now waiting and the position that must decide, or the final status.
Every action is written to the flow log: who, when, which step, the note.
steps: Finds the active flow configuration of the module (and division).
Picks the first step whose status-from and amount range match.
Finds who decides: the holder of the position, or the person acting for it within the acting dates.
Approve looks for the next matching step; none left = the flow is finished.
Steps of kind AUTO or NOTIFY ONLY are executed without waiting.

entries.note: Confirm on the screen = send the order to the approval flow; null = success, otherwise the message.
Runs when the last approval passes: the order becomes Confirmed and the schedule is created.

name: CPDEL Engine (Customer Plan Delivery)
purpose: Creates the delivery schedule when a Customer Order is confirmed.
inputs: The Customer Order with its lines.
Required on every product line before Confirm.
outputs: One line per product line: full quantity on the due date.
Submitted, then Confirmed after the last approval.
steps: Refuses when a product line has no due date (or, for an order without quotation, no Master Product), or when a product still has more than one quantity line to choose from.
Sends the order to the Flow Engine (CO).
After the last approval, creates one delivery line per product line that has no manual schedule yet.
Lines already scheduled by hand are not touched.
Sales can then Split or Join the lines on the CPDEL screen.

entries.note: Row colour by working days left to the slot.
Why a slot is not valid; empty = valid.
PPIC: when the goods will be ready; later than the slot needs a reason.
Sales: the new slot agreed with the customer, may split part of the quantity.
Sales: the customer refused, escalate to the Operational Manager.
Operational Manager: overtime, priority, subcontract or a new offer.

name: CPDEL Two Promises
purpose: Keeps the promise to the customer (delivery slot) and the promise of production (ready date) in line.
inputs: The form values of the action: date, time, reason, quantity to split.
outputs: WAITING_PPIC, ALIGNED, NEED_NEGOTIATION, ESCALATED, LATE or SHIPPED.
Past = red, today = orange, soon = yellow, shipped = grey.
Every action is recorded; the first promised date never changes.
steps: A slot is valid only inside Telasih office hours, the customer receiving hours and on a working day.
PPIC fills the ready date; when it is later than the slot the line asks Sales to negotiate.
Sales records the new slot (or a split) agreed by WhatsApp or phone.
A refusal goes to the Operational Manager, whose decision sends the line back to PPIC.

entries.note: The whole picture: every demand line and every material with its coverage.
Step 1: what must be made and when.
Step 2: the materials one demand needs.
Saves the proposed booking of a confirmed order (Draft, soft).
PPIC locks the booking: stock is reserved per location.
Back to Draft: stock is released and the plan recalculated.
Recalculates every order (button, nightly command, order changes).
PPIC chooses the stock item for a line that only has a specification.
Pre-booking: recalculates the soft bookings of costed inquiries that have no Customer Order yet, and releases those whose chain ended.

name: Material Planning Engine (MPS · MRP · Booking)
purpose: Works out which materials every order needs, books stock for it and shows what is short.
inputs: Active Customer Orders: Confirmed = firm; Draft / Submitted = shown only.
The rest of the MPS forecast after the orders of the same month.
The earlier of the delivery date and order date plus the working days in BOOKING_NEED_WORKDAYS.
Available stock, open Purchase Orders and Requisitions with their dates.
outputs: Per demand and material: needed, covered by stock / PO / PR, short.
Per material: total need, available, first needed, order by (latest), coverage status.
One booking document per order (Draft or Confirmed).
steps: Finished goods stock of the same product is booked first.
The rest is broken down into all materials: paper from the Pro-Dev layout, then costing, then BOM; ink, varnish, coating, film and glue from the usage standards.
Netting per material: Confirmed first, then Draft, then Forecast, each by need date.
Supply is used in this order: available stock, PO on time, PR, late PO / PR, then SHORT.
A booking confirmed by PPIC is frozen: read from the database, not recalculated.

Pre-booking (runPre): from the moment costing has calculated, a soft booking (stage B0 / B1, shown as Not CO yet) is written per inquiry without a Customer Order. When the CO is Confirmed it takes over that header; when costing is reversed, the quotation expires or the inquiry is cancelled, the pre-booking is cancelled.
The engine only reads master data; it writes bookings and requisitions only.

entries.note: Every item that has stock in a bin now, with its arrival date, its last real movement and the dead stock flag.
Per bin: its items, weight and volume in use, percent of capacity, status, pallets, the stack, and whether it holds dead, expired, remnant or buried stock.
Per bin: its labelled pallets and packs from the top down, each with its stack number, age, estimated height and the marks remnant, old remnant and buried.
Per bin: floor area, stacking height, volume and the stack limit, taken from the storage area and the building.
Estimated weight of a quantity; empty when it cannot be estimated.
Estimated volume of a quantity of sheets; empty when it cannot be estimated.
Estimated height of one pallet or pack in a stack; empty when it cannot be estimated.
Number of sheets of a quantity when the unit is sheets or reams; empty for other units.
From how many sheets or fewer a labelled unit counts as a remnant.
The dead stock limit in months.
From which percent of its capacity a bin counts as Full.
How many days before the expiry date a pallet is tagged Expires soon.

name: Warehouse Stock (bins, capacity, dead stock)
purpose: Tells what is in every bin, how full the bin is by weight and by volume, when the goods arrived, and which stock is dead or expired. One source for the Warehouse Map, transfers, labels and tracking.
inputs: The bins to read; empty = every bin.
Only these items, per stock class (used when tracking one item).
The bin rows with their capacity, storage area and usable flag.
The active labelled pallets and packs, grouped per bin.
outputs: Per bin the units from the top down: stack number (1 = bottom), pallet or pack, quantity, age, estimated height, and the marks remnant, old remnant and buried.
Class, item, bin, quantity, unit, value, estimated weight and volume, arrival date, last movement, idle days, dead flag.
Floor area (m2), stacking height (m) and volume (m3) of the bin.
EMPTY, IN_USE, FULL (weight or volume at the Full percent or more), OVER (above capacity) or BLOCKED.
steps: Reads the stock balance views of raw material, semi finished and finished goods: the last stock card row per item and bin.
Arrival date = the latest stock-in or opening row of the item in that bin; a bin filled only by transfers uses the latest arrival of the item anywhere.
Last movement = the latest stock card row of the item in any bin that is not a stock transfer, so moving stock never resets it.
Dead stock = that movement is older than the limit, or the item never moved. The same rule as the assistant answer and the Deadstock widget.
Bin size: floor area = area of the storage area divided by its positions; height = stacking height of the area (or the clear height of the floor) divided by the rack levels; volume = area x height.

Weight: unit KG = the quantity; sheets with grammage and size = sheets x gsm x length x width. Volume: sheets x length x width x thickness (thickness from the master, or grammage x the paper bulk constant). Anything else is unknown and left out of the capacity.
How full a bin is = the higher of the weight percent and the volume percent.
Expiry of a bin comes from its pallet labels: Expired, or Expires soon within the number of days in the constant.
Stack: on a rack the level is the bin. On the floor every labelled unit has a stack number in its bin, 1 = bottom. A pack is a remnant; an old remnant arrived longer ago than the dead stock limit.

Buried = the unit to use first for its item (a remnant first, then the earliest expiry, then the oldest arrival, compared with every unit of the item in any bin) has another pallet on top of it. A twin pallet of the same arrival does not count.

Stack height = the sum of the unit heights (sheets x thickness, plus the wooden pallet) against the stacking height of the bin. A bin with more pallets than the stack limit of its area is marked; an empty limit only monitors.
Stock in a bin that is not on a label has no known place in the stack and is reported as Stack not recorded.
settings: Settings > Constants: ASSISTANT_DEADSTOCK_MONTHS, WH_BIN_FULL_PCT, WH_PAPER_BULK_CM3_PER_G, WH_EXPIRY_SOON_DAYS, WH_REMNANT_MAX_SHEETS, WH_PALLET_BASE_CM
Inventory > Warehouse > Buildings: clear height per floor
Inventory > Warehouse > Storage Areas: stack height, max. stacked pallets

entries.note: Posts one stock document. Refused as a whole when a balance would go below zero or the date is in a closed inventory period.

name: Stock Document Posting (stock card order)
purpose: Writes a stock document (Stock In, Out, Return, Adjustment, goods receipt and its reversal) to the stock card in document-date order and keeps every later balance right.
inputs: Stock class: RM, SFG or FG.
The stock document (header with its lines: item, bin, quantity, unit price).
outputs: One row per document line, placed by document date; all later rows of that item in that bin are recalculated.
True when it worked; otherwise the reason, and nothing is written.
Usage journal lines that could not be made because an account is missing.
How many later stock-out rows got another average price and by how much their value changed; their journals are not changed.
steps: Refuses a document that was posted or cancelled before, and a document dated in a closed inventory period (the correction is a Stock Adjustment dated in an open period).
Per line inserts a stock card row at its place: after every row with the same or an earlier date, before rows dated later.
Recalculates that row and all later rows of the item in that bin: opening balance, closing balance, moving average price, value (StockCardChain).
A receipt changes the average price (weighted with the stock before it); stock out, adjustment and transfer rows carry the average price of the row before.
When the average price of a transfer-out row changes, the value that moved is corrected in the destination bin and that bin is recalculated too.
When the new row or a later row would go below zero the whole document is refused (adjustments and physical counts are exempt, as before).
Marks the document Posted, updates the item total on the master, then makes the usage journal for real stock-out lines.
A posted document is never changed; a mistake is corrected with a Stock Adjustment.

entries.note: Why the transfer cannot be confirmed yet; empty = it can.
Approval switched off: moves the stock. Approval switched on: sends the transfer for approval.
Gives the document its number and puts it in the approval queue; the stock does not move yet.
Moves the stock: from a Draft, or after the last approval.
Moves the stock back to the source bins, or withdraws a transfer that still waits for approval; needs a reason.
Stock value of the transfer, used for the approval limits.
Stock of one item in one bin right now.
Two-step transfer, step 1: moves the stock from the source bin to the In Transit bin and confirms the document. Returns an error text or null.
Two-step transfer, step 2: moves the received quantity from In Transit to the destination bin; a shortage stays in In Transit as a discrepancy.
Settles a received-short line: write it off to the Loss bin, or return it to the source bin.

name: Stock Transfer Posting
purpose: Moves stock from one bin to another, in the same warehouse or between warehouses, with or without approval, and can take the move back.
inputs: The transfer document with its lines: item, source bin, destination bin, quantity.
True when called after the last approval.
outputs: Two rows per line: out of the source bin and into the destination bin, both marked TF.
TF + year + running number, issued at Confirm.
Labelled pallets and packs follow the stock to the destination bin and go on top of the stack there.
Empty when it worked; otherwise the reason, and nothing is written.
steps: Checks every line: quantity, destination bin in the destination warehouse, bin not blocked, enough stock in the source bin (lines from the same bin are added up).

Approval (Setup > Security > Approval Levels, module TF) is switched off by default. Switched on: Confirm only sends the transfer for approval and the stock moves when the last level approves; a rejected transfer never moves stock.
Per line writes the row out of the source bin and the row into the destination bin; the value moves with the average price of the source bin.
The destination bin gets a weighted average price. The total stock of the item does not change and no journal is made.
Notes on the line whether the item was dead stock at that moment.

Pallets follow: a line made from one pallet moves that pallet; a line that empties the bin moves all its pallets; otherwise the oldest pallets move when their quantities add up exactly, else they stay and the label work list shows the difference.
Cancel writes the same two rows the other way round and brings the pallets back; it stops when the stock is no longer in the destination bin.

Two-step transfer (In Transit): Ship moves the stock to the virtual In Transit bin and numbers the document; Receive moves what arrived to the destination bin. Quantity not received stays in In Transit until Loss or Return settles it. No journal and no approval.
settings: Setup > Security > Approval Levels: module TF (switched off by default)

entries.note: Uses the batch of this item and supplier lot if it exists, otherwise creates it. Attributes are used only when creating.
Creates a batch with the next batch number; the status starts as given (Released by default).
Changes the quality status after sampling, first article or a usage decision. Rejected and Blocked need a reason.
The batch of an item and supplier lot; upper and lower case and edge spaces are not told apart.
True when stock of this batch may be picked. Stock without a batch (old data) counts as allowed.
Label, tone, available and allocatable flags of one status.
True for a raw material with a shelf life: a new batch then needs an expiry date.
Upper case, trimmed lot; an empty lot becomes the constant INV_NO_LOT_BATCH_CODE.
Finds the item (raw material, part or product) by its code, with its shelf life.

name: Batch Service (batch master and quality status)
purpose: The one door for creating batches and changing their quality status. Screens, receiving, backfill and QC all call it; nothing writes the batch table directly.
inputs: Stock class: RM, SFG or FG.
Lot number written by the supplier; may be empty.
Optional: part, supplier, production and expiry date, quality status, certification, food grade, grain direction, notes.
The new status; the reason is required for Rejected and Blocked.
outputs: One batch per class, item and lot, with a batch number and a quality status.
Whether stock of the batch counts as Available and whether it may be allocated.
steps: A batch is one class + item + supplier lot. The same lot is never made twice.
Statuses: Quarantine (not available), Conditional (available, with a mark), Released, Rejected and Blocked (neither available nor allocatable).
Only setStatus changes the status, and every change keeps who and when.
Rejected or Blocked without a reason is refused.

entries.note: With write = false it only counts what would be created and linked.

name: Batch Backfill (batches from old lot data)
purpose: Turns the lot numbers already in stock cards and pallets into batches and links the old rows to them. Safe to run twice; a check run only counts.
inputs: False = check only, nothing is written.
Name recorded on the new batches.
Limit to these stock classes; empty = RM, SFG and FG.
Limit to these items; empty = all.
outputs: Batches created and already existing, lot spellings merged, and rows linked per stock class.
batch_id filled on stock cards, document lines and pallets that had none.
steps: Groups the existing rows by class, item and lot (upper case, edge spaces removed).
An empty lot belongs to the batch named by INV_NO_LOT_BATCH_CODE.
Uses the batch of that group if it exists, otherwise creates it as Released with the nearest pallet expiry date.
Fills batch_id only on rows that have none, so a second run changes nothing.
writes: batch_id of stock cards, document lines and pallets

entries.note: Up to a limit of bins that follow the rules, with free weight and the reason for the suggestion.
Marks a bin as used by this pallet so the next suggestion of the same run does not overfill it.
Dock to line: the bin in a WIP area (then Staging) for a pallet that goes straight to production.

name: Putaway Planner (suggests a bin)
purpose: Suggests the bins where a received pallet may be put away, best first. The warehouse officer confirms by scanning; the planner never moves stock.
inputs: The pallet to put away, with its item, quantity, batch and current bin.
Its batch; a Rejected, Blocked or Quarantine batch gets no suggestion.
Work order for dock to line.
outputs: Bin, storage area, whether the bin is empty, free kilograms and a short reason.
A WIP or Staging bin, or nothing when the area has none.
steps: Only batches that may be allocated are put away.
Active Storage areas that are not virtual and whose stock class fits (Any or the class of the pallet).
Active, usable bins that are not locked for counting and follow the Mixing rule of the area.
Capacity check by weight, number of pallets and the stack limit of the area; a weight that cannot be estimated does not refuse a bin.
Order: same building as the pallet first, area order, empty bins first, then bin code.

entries.note: Creates a task for each pallet still in a receiving or QC Hold area and cancels the tasks whose pallet has moved.
Waiting (Quarantine), Ready, To line (Conditional: dock to line) or Blocked (Rejected, Blocked) from the batch quality.
The bins of the Putaway Planner for one task.
The officer scans the pallet then the bin; the stock moves through a real Stock Transfer document.

name: Warehouse Task Service (putaway tasks)
purpose: Keeps the list of putaway tasks for pallets that wait in a receiving or QC Hold area and moves the pallet when the officer scans it and its bin.
inputs: Required when the bin differs from the suggestion.
outputs: Status Open, Done or Cancelled, with the bin used and who and when.
The document that moved the pallet; balances change only there.
steps: Sync is run when Receiving & Putaway opens; one open task per pallet.
A task is Urgent when the pallet comes from a receipt line marked URGENT.
Confirm refuses a wrong pallet or bin scan and a task that is Waiting or Blocked.
A bin other than the suggested ones needs a reason. Putaway is an internal bin move: the Stock Transfer approval is not used.

entries.note: The pallets to take for a needed quantity; what is not covered comes back as SHORT.
All pallets that may be used, in pick order.
Why a batch may not be picked for this need; null = it may.
Owner (company or customer) of the stock in one bin and batch.

name: Pick Allocator (which pallet to take)
purpose: For one material, chooses the pallets, batches and bins that may be taken and in which order. The warehouse officer confirms by scanning.
inputs: Grain direction, certification and food grade asked by the booking.
outputs: Pallet, batch, bin and quantity per piece of the need.
The quantity that no pallet could cover. Material is never invented.
steps: Only active pallets in usable bins that are not locked for counting, in Storage or Consignment areas.
Only batches that may be allocated; Conditional only for class B and C material (never food grade, FSC or PEFC), and INV_PICK_CONDITIONAL_ALLOWED = 0 switches it off.
Expired batches and batches that do not fit the grain or certification are skipped.
Stock owned by someone else is skipped, except the customer of that order.
Order per area follows its Pick Order: FIFO (oldest first) or FEFO (earliest expiry first).
Pallets already allocated to another open pick list are subtracted.

entries.note: Makes the list from the Confirmed booking of the work order; lines that cannot be covered are SHORT.
Recalculates the lines that are not scanned yet, after stock arrived or a batch changed.
Confirms the right pallet for a line.
Confirms the right bin; the line becomes PICKED.
One scan box: finds out whether the code is a pallet or a bin and applies it.
All lines picked: posts Stock Out RM to the work order (one document per warehouse) and marks the list DONE.
Cancels before DONE; only the allocation is released because no stock moved yet.

name: Pick List Service
purpose: Makes a pick list per Work Order from its confirmed booking, lets the officer scan pallets and bins, and issues the material to the work order when all lines are picked.
inputs: Where the material is delivered; empty = default.
The pallet or bin code scanned.
outputs: Lines with pallet, batch, bin, quantity and status.
Posted by the normal stock posting when the list is confirmed.
Issued quantity of the booking lines goes up; used pallets are relabelled.
steps: Needs a Confirmed booking for the work order.
The Pick Allocator chooses pallets, batches and bins; the officer confirms by scanning, never by trusting the suggestion.
Confirm writes no stock card itself: it calls the stock document and posting services, so balances stay owned by Inventory.
The leftover reservation is released when the work order ends.

entries.note: With dryRun = true it only lists what would happen.

name: Booking Maintenance (hold and stale booking)
purpose: Frees reservations nobody uses: a Hold that has expired, and a Confirmed booking that never became a work order.
inputs: Date to judge from; empty = today.
outputs: Booking numbers whose Hold expired and was released.
Booking numbers marked Stale: no work order a while after the need date.
Booking numbers released: no work order long after the need date.
steps: A HELD booking whose hold date has passed is released.
A Confirmed booking with a Customer Order and no work order is warned (Stale) after INV_BOOKING_STALE_WARN_DAYS days past the need date.
After INV_BOOKING_STALE_RELEASE_DAYS days it is released and the stock is Available again.
A booking with any issued quantity or an existing work order is never released.

entries.note: The whole plan: risk class, intensity and sample size.
A (high risk), B (standard) or C (low risk) of the item.
Pass and reject history of a supplier, read from the sampling decisions.
Pieces to sample for an intensity and a lot quantity; Skip = certificate only.

name: QC Sampling Service (sampling plan)
purpose: Works out how a received lot is checked: the risk class of the item, how tight the checks are for this supplier, and the sample size for the lot.
outputs: Risk class, intensity (Tightened, Normal, Reduced or Skip) and sample size.
steps: Risk class: the item first, then its category, the deepest category wins; with no data it is B.
Starting intensity follows the class. A new supplier (fewer decided lots than INV_QC_NEW_SUPPLIER_LOTS) starts Tightened.
After a reject the supplier stays Tightened until enough lots in a row pass; enough passes in a row move it to Reduced.
Sample size comes from the sampling plan table by intensity and lot range; Skip = 0 (certificate only). It never exceeds the lot.
Shortage events do not yet count in the history.
settings: Quality Setup: Sampling Plan, Sampling Rules, Risk Class

entries.note: Records the decision, changes the batch status and, when rejected or blocked, holds the work orders and opens a supplier claim.
Records the first article result of a work order for a batch.
How long a batch has waited for a decision.

name: QC Decision Service
purpose: The one door for a quality decision on a batch: sampling at the dock, first article at the press, a later usage decision, or a deviation. Each decision changes the batch status and is kept.
inputs: Sampling at dock, First article, Usage decision or Deviation.
Released, Rejected, Blocked or Conditional use.
Who decides. The right to decide is checked by the caller (QcAuthority).
outputs: Type, decision, reason, who and when; the sampling history of the supplier is read from it.
Work orders that used a rejected batch are held and one supplier claim is opened.
steps: Each decision sets the batch status through the Batch Service and writes one decision row.
Rejected or Blocked needs a reason; the work orders that used the batch are held and a supplier claim is opened (QC Trace Service).
A later decision that is not Rejected or Blocked releases the holds.
The right to decide is not checked here, so screens and tests use the same path.

entries.note: Batch to issue documents to work orders to Customer Orders and deliveries.
Holds the work orders and opens the claim for a rejected or blocked batch.
Puts a hold on every work order that used the batch.
Opens one claim to the supplier of the batch.
Frees the holds when the batch is later decided as not rejected.
Moves a supplier claim to its next status.

name: QC Trace Service (forward trace of a rejected batch)
purpose: Finds where a rejected batch went: the issue documents, the work orders, and the orders or deliveries made from it; holds those work orders and opens one supplier claim.
inputs: Why it was rejected or blocked.
The claim to update and its new status.
outputs: The work orders, orders and deliveries that used the batch.
One hold per affected work order.
steps: Issue lines carry the batch; old issue lines without a batch are matched by item and supplier lot.
Every work order that used the batch is held and the number of held orders is reported.
One claim is opened for the supplier, not one per work order.
The holds are freed again if the batch is later decided as not rejected or blocked.

entries.note: Marks a stock line URGENT with a reason and the work order that needs it.
Takes the mark and its approval away.
Head of QC or an operations manager approves an FSC, PEFC or food grade URGENT line.
Sets the certification and food grade claim of the line.
True for FSC, PEFC or food grade material (switch INV_URGENT_FSC_APPROVAL).
What still stops the line from being posted.
Makes the batch of the URGENT lines before posting.

name: Urgent Receipt Service
purpose: Lets a receipt line be posted before the quality result and go straight to production (URGENT), while sampling runs in parallel and the batch stays Conditional.
inputs: The work order that needs the material.
Who acts: PPIC, production supervisor or manager, operations manager for the mark; head of QC or operations manager for approval.
outputs: Who, when, why and which work order, on the receipt line.
The receipt may post although the quality result is pending; the batch is born Conditional.
steps: Only an authorised person can mark; it needs a reason of 5 characters and an existing work order.
Changing the reason or the work order removes an earlier approval.
A line with FSC, PEFC or food grade needs approval before posting, when INV_URGENT_FSC_APPROVAL is 1.
The line is no longer blocked by the pending quality result; its batch is Conditional and sampling goes on in Conditional Stock.

entries.note: The suspected shortage of one comparison: issued minus output and standard waste.
Tolerance of the PO line of the receipt; empty = RECEIVE_TOLERANCE_PCT.
The comparison of one work order and material.
The work order and material pairs that can be compared.

name: Shortage Detector (short delivery found late)
purpose: Compares the material issued to a work order with its good output plus standard waste and suspects a short delivery when material is missing.
inputs: Material issued to the work order, net of returns, in material unit.
Good output in material unit, typed by the officer.
Standard waste of the work order.
Tolerance percent of the PO line.
outputs: Quantity above the tolerance; zero when it is within tolerance.
steps: Suspected shortage = net issued - (good output + standard waste).
Actual waste above standard is usage variance, not a short delivery.
Only a suspicion above the tolerance becomes a request; the head of the warehouse must recount before it counts.
Good output in material unit is typed by the officer, or filled from production data by the Shortage Auto Detector (inv:detect-shortage).

entries.note: Makes a Draft request from a suspected shortage.
The head of the warehouse recounts or reweighs; the confirmed shortage is the proof.
Closes the suspicion as usage variance.
PPIC confirms: received quantity goes down, the PO line reopens, GR/IR is corrected and stock is reduced.
Purchasing tells the source; the sending window starts.
The shortfall arrived through a normal receipt.
The source refuses or the window lapsed: the PO line closes at the received quantity.
Finishes the request.
Closes requests whose window has passed.
True when a receipt has shortage corrections.

name: Shortage Request Service (send us the shortfall)
purpose: Follows a short delivery from suspicion to settlement: recount, confirm, ask the supplier, subcontractor or customer to send the shortfall, and close or refuse.
inputs: Source (supplier, subcontractor, customer), receipt line, work order and suspected quantity.
The recount and the confirmed shortage.
Evidence or reason of each step.
outputs: Draft, Confirmed, Sent, Received, Refused or Closed with its outcome.
Lower received quantity, reopened PO line, GR/IR correction (PV_SHORT) and a Stock Out ref PV_SHORT.
The PO line is closed at the received quantity and marked as needing a debit note.
steps: Draft from a suspicion above the PO tolerance, then recount as proof or dismiss as usage variance.

Confirm lowers the received quantity, reopens the PO line as backorder, corrects GR/IR and reduces the stock; a subcontractor receipt uses its own shortage report and customer material changes quantity only.
Send tells the source; it has INV_SHORTAGE_WINDOW_DAYS days to send the shortfall.
Received closes the request; a refusal or a lapsed window closes the PO line at the received quantity (CLOSED_SHORT).

Notices go to the head of the warehouse (new), PPIC (recounted) and Purchasing (confirmed); a Draft purchase request is made on Confirm and a Draft debit note on Refuse (ShortageFollowUp). The debit note has no journal yet.

entries.note: Checks every work order and material that has material issued (or one work order); a dry run writes nothing.
Judges one work order and material and returns CREATED, WOULD_CREATE, COVERED, WITHIN_TOLERANCE or SKIPPED with the reason.
Good output and standard waste in the material unit, or the reason they cannot be known.

name: Shortage Auto Detector (from production output)
purpose: Fills the good output and the standard waste from production data and makes a Draft shortage request when material issued exceeds them by more than the PO tolerance.
inputs: Who is recorded on the requests.
outputs: One row per work order and material with its state and the suspected quantity.
A shortage request marked AUTO, and a notice to the head of the warehouse.
steps: Good output in material unit = material need of the work order x (good output of the last operation / work order quantity).
The need already holds the standard waste of all steps, so the check does not accuse; cutting waste is added on top.
Suspected shortage = net issued - (good output + standard waste); only a gap above the PO tolerance of the receipt line becomes a request.
The receipt line comes from the batches issued to the work order; a pair is skipped when the work order is not finished, has no output or need, uses another unit, or the issue has no batch.

entries.note: Why the document cannot be reversed; null = it can.
Whether the document is reversed, and by which document.
Posts the reversing document and marks the original Cancelled.
Makes a new Draft copy of a document, to post it again corrected.
The reason text suggested for a document.

name: Stock Reversal Service (cancel a posted stock document)
purpose: Cancels a posted stock document without editing or deleting it: a reversing document with the opposite direction is posted through the normal path.
inputs: Stock class: RM, SFG or FG.
outputs: Category REVERSAL with the number prefix RV, opposite direction, referring to the original.
Status Cancelled, pointing to its reversal.
Chains on: BB equals the previous EB; the average follows the normal chain.
The usage journal of a Stock Out RM or SFG is reversed too.
steps: Refused as a whole when the inventory period is closed or the balance would turn negative.
Refused for Adjustment, Opname and opening balance (own paths), documents of other processes such as a receipt (cancel it there) and a reversal itself.
A reversed Stock Out returns the goods at the value it left; a reversed Stock In leaves at the current average price.
The original is never edited or deleted; a copy can be made as a Draft.
reads: tm2inv.rm_stock / sfg_stock / fg_stock and their lines
used: Stock Out, Return and Stock In screens (Cancel)

entries.note: Areas never counted or last counted more than their Count Every days ago, without an open count.
Starts the count of every due area; returns the number of new tasks.
Makes one task per item in a bin for one area and locks those bins.
The officer types the counted quantity; the difference with the stock card posts as a Stock Opname document.
Cancels the task without adjustment.

name: Count Task Service (cycle count)
purpose: Makes count tasks for storage areas that are due, locks their bins while counting, and turns the difference into a Stock Opname document.
inputs: The count task and the quantity counted.
outputs: One per item per bin, with the system quantity.
Transfer to or from a locked bin is refused; putaway and pick skip it.
Document category OP for the differences, posted like any adjustment.
steps: An area is due when it is active, not virtual, has Count Every days and that time has passed.
Start makes a task for each position with stock and locks the bins of the area.
Confirm compares the counted quantity with the stock card balance of that moment and posts the difference.
A bin is opened again when no open count task is left in it. A closed period refuses the posting as usual.

entries.note: Moves material from a warehouse bin to the vendor bin through a Stock Transfer.
Unused material comes back to a warehouse bin.
Material used at the vendor: a normal Stock Out RM from the vendor bin.
A Subcontract receipt uses material in proportion to the quantity received from the PO line.
Cancels a send while nothing was used or returned.

name: Subcontract Stock Service (material at the vendor)
purpose: Sends raw material to a subcontractor against a Subcontract PO and keeps the material at the vendor as our own stock until it is used or comes back.
inputs: The open Subcontract PO and its line.
Where the material leaves, which one and how much.
outputs: Document with lines per material and the quantity sent, used and returned.
The vendor bin holds the stock, still owned by the company and valued at the average of the source bin.
Standard usage journal when the material is consumed.
steps: The PO must be a Subcontract PO that is not finished.
Send is a Stock Transfer to the virtual bin of that vendor, so the stock card, value and pallets behave like a transfer; no journal.
Consume is a Stock Out RM from the vendor bin, so usage is booked in the standard way.
A receipt of the subcontract product reduces the vendor balance in proportion to the received quantity.
Only raw material is supported; semi finished and finished goods to a subcontractor are not built.

entries.note: Puts the stock lines of the receipt into the consignment bin as stock owned by the customer; returns the stock document id.
The consignment bin of a warehouse.
The lines of the receipt that point to a raw material.

name: Customer Material Service (consignment)
purpose: Turns the material a customer brings (a Customer receipt with a raw material item) into stock owned by that customer, kept in a consignment bin, without value and without journal.
inputs: Warehouse of the consignment bin; empty = default.
outputs: Raw material stock with owner CUSTOMER in a Customer Consignment area.
No price, no stock value and no journal.
steps: Only lines that point to a raw material become stock; a line with a description only stays a note.
The stock posting already treats an owner other than the company as not valued and not journalled.
The Pick Allocator lets this stock be picked only for work of that customer.
writes: Stock In RM document with owner CUSTOMER

entries.note: The virtual warehouse (code VIRT).
The virtual area of a type: Loss, In Transit or At Subcontractor.
The one Loss bin.
The one In Transit bin.
The bin of one subcontractor.
Makes the warehouse, the areas and the Loss and In Transit bins.

name: Virtual Location Service (Loss, In Transit, vendor bins)
purpose: Makes the places where stock exists in the books but not on the warehouse floor: Loss, In Transit and one bin per subcontractor. Created when needed, never twice.
inputs: The subcontractor, for a vendor bin.
outputs: A bin in a virtual area. Calling again returns the same row.
steps: One virtual warehouse holds three areas: Loss (one bin), In Transit (one bin) and At Subcontractor (one bin per supplier).
Everything is created on demand and is idempotent.
Virtual areas are not on the Warehouse Map and get no bins from Generate Bins.

entries.note: Every stock position with its labelled pallets and what is still to do: arrival label or relabel.
Makes the pallets of an arrival: quantity, supplier pallet code, lot and expiry date per pallet.
Replaces the quantity of a pallet with what is left after use; zero closes the pallet and the units above it move down. A small remainder becomes a remnant pack.
Swaps a unit with the one above or below it in the stack of its bin. No stock document: the bin and the quantity do not change.
Renumbers the stack of one bin to 1, 2, 3 without gaps, keeping the order.
Pallet or pack: what the officer chose, otherwise a pack when sheet goods are at or below the remnant limit.
Counts a reprint of a pallet label.
Moves the pallets that belong to a confirmed stock transfer.
Brings those pallets back when the transfer is cancelled.
The items and bins of one posted goods receipt, with what is not on a pallet label yet.
Arrival date plus the shelf life of the item; empty when the item has no shelf life.

name: Pallet Labels (arrival label, relabel after use)
purpose: Keeps one label per pallet and tells which stock still needs a pallet label: goods that arrived without one, and pallets whose label no longer matches because stock was used.
inputs: The bins to look at; empty = every bin.
One stock position: class, item, part and bin.
The new pallets: quantity, supplier pallet code, lot number, expiry date.
Arrival date, receipt number, a note and the unit kind (pallet, pack or automatic) for all new pallets.
up or down: where the unit goes in the stack.
Pallet or pack; empty = decided from the remnant limit.
What is left on the pallet.
outputs: Per stock position: on hand, quantity on pallet labels, the difference, and Arrival label or Relabel after use.
Pallet number PL + year + running number, its kind (pallet or pack), its stack number in the bin, and its history: created, relabelled, moved, restacked, closed.
Why pallets cannot be made or relabelled, for example more than what is in the bin.
steps: The stock card stays the only truth for quantities. A pallet is a labelled physical unit inside that stock and never changes it.
Per item and bin compares the stock on hand with the total quantity on active pallet labels.
More stock than labels = goods arrived without a pallet label. Less stock than labels = stock was used and a label still shows the old quantity.
New pallets may not add up to more than the unlabelled quantity. The expiry date is proposed from the arrival date and the shelf life of the item; the officer may change it.
The engine only shows the difference; the officer decides which pallet holds how much.

Stack number: 1 = bottom. New units go on top in the order they are made; a unit that arrives by stock transfer goes on top in the destination bin; when a unit is used up or leaves, the units above it move down.
Remnant: a unit of sheet goods (unit LBR or RIM, 1 ream = 500 sheets) at or below WH_REMNANT_MAX_SHEETS becomes a pack; the officer may also choose pallet or pack. A pack is not counted as a pallet.

entries.note: The ledger of one period (first and last date).
Every stock card row of the period by date, with its value and the running balance of the item.
One row per item and bin that had stock before the period or moved in it.
One row per item: all its bins added up.

name: Stock Period Ledger
purpose: Works out the stock of a period for the reports: opening balance, movements and closing balance of every item, in quantity and value, for all stock classes.
outputs: Quantity and value just before the first date and at the end of the last date.
Quantity and value of the period, per kind of movement. Stock transfers are kept apart.
Document, kind of movement, bin, quantity, value and the balance of the item after it.
steps: Opening balance of an item in a bin = its last stock card row before the first date.
Reads the stock card rows of the period in date order. In, Out and Adjustment come from the row; a stock transfer changes the bin, not the item.
Value of a movement = value of the bin after the row minus its value before, so opening + in - out + adjustment always equals closing.
Closing balance = the last row of the period, or the opening balance when nothing moved.

name: Work Order Generation
purpose: Creates the Work Orders when a delivery line is posted to Production.
inputs: One delivery line of a Confirmed and approved Customer Order.
outputs: One per part of the product, with operations (routing) and materials. A product without parts gets one simple Work Order for PPIC to complete.
steps: Refuses when the line already has Work Orders, the order is not Confirmed and approved, or the line has no Master Product.
One inquiry part = one Work Order.
Operations and materials come from the Spec Engine for this quantity.
Target rates are taken from the product and part code.

entries.note: The waiting jobs of one machine, in order.
The job that should start now; null when its crew is not available.
Target start and finish per operation; not saved.
Checks a drag / resize on the board; empty list = allowed.

name: PDR Engine (Scheduling)
purpose: Decides which job a machine should run next and plans a Work Order backwards from its due date.
inputs: The crew PPIC wants to assign.
The moment to judge from (default: now).
The Work Order to plan backwards.
A manual move on the Scheduling Board.
outputs: Jobs or groups of jobs, highest priority first.
Target start and finish per operation.
Why a manual move is refused.
steps: Batching: jobs that can run together (same dieline ...) become one unit.
Priority score in layers: hot job, critical ratio, earliest due date, resource fit, first in first out.
Sequencing: smooths the order among jobs of equal priority only.
Crew check: the top job is skipped when its crew is not on shift.
Backward scheduling: from the due date back through the operations, using the rate band of each process and the machine calendar.

name: Scheduling Rule Engine
purpose: Applies the batching and sequencing rules kept as data, not as code.
inputs: The operations waiting for a machine.
The same list after the priority score.
The resource the rules belong to.
outputs: Lists of operations; a group of one = no batching fits.
The list reordered inside equal priorities.
steps: Reads the active rules of the resource.
Batching joins operations of different Work Orders that share the rule key.
Sequencing rules are applied oldest rule first as the main key, later rules as tie breakers.
The priority order (hot job, critical ratio, due date) is never changed.

name: Job Order Learning (Sequence)
purpose: Learns the order in which the officer applies jobs to the Live Schedule and suggests that order for new jobs on a machine.
inputs: The machine whose waiting Draft jobs are ordered.
The officer arrangement recorded at PROCESS (TRIAL, context only) and at APPLY (FINAL, the training label).
outputs: The Draft jobs of the machine, best first, with the place each has now.
Decision pairs learned against the 30 needed, and the accuracy against the engine order on the newest 20% of APPLYs.
steps: PROCESS stores a TRIAL snapshot of the machine order; the next PROCESS replaces it. APPLY turns the last arrangement into a FINAL label.
Six features per job: urgency (due date minus work hours), priority, duration, similarity to the job before it, material gate, wait before.
sequence:train fits a pairwise linear ranking (logistic regression, L2) on the FINAL pairs; jobs that came from a suggestion are not used.
The model is ACTIVE only with at least 30 pairs and a better pair accuracy than the engine order on the newest 20% of APPLYs; otherwise the screen shows Learning n / 30.
USE moves the jobs through the same pending move as a drag and stays DRAFT; DISMISS is logged as SEQ_REJECT. A job with a problem or a machine that is down is recorded as context.
used: Work Order form > Simulation and QUE

name: Hot Job Option Generator
purpose: When an urgent job must be inserted, proposes up to three ways to do it with their measured impact.
outputs: One to three options; each shows which job moves, by how many hours, and whether it stays safe.
The option PPIC chose is recorded.
steps: Takes the waiting queue of the machine from the PDR Engine.
For the first two waiting jobs: "insert and move this job", with the delay in hours (the duration of the urgent job) and whether the moved job still meets its due date (safe / at risk).
Always adds a last option: send the urgent job to a subcontractor, so no job moves (needs a subcontract Purchase Order).
Shows the options; PPIC decides. There is no automatic answer.

name: Speed Target Engine
purpose: Proposes the target speed of every machine and of every process x machine pair.
inputs: Per machine: its data, its own output history and its process pairs.
The target filled in now (for the decision whether to propose).
outputs: A suggestion: speed, source, confidence (Low / Medium / High), sample size.
A suggestion per process x machine pair that has its own history.
steps: Sources are tried in order; the first that gives a number wins: v2 output, old-system output of the machine, old-system output of the process, same machine model, ratio to similar machines, the model specification, the process default.
Pass 1 uses the history of each machine; pass 2 lets machines without history borrow from the others.
A pair is proposed only from its own history; without it, it inherits the machine target.
PPIC is asked only when the target is empty, or the difference is larger than the minimum percentage with at least Medium confidence.
The engine never reads or writes the database itself: a repository loads the data, a store keeps the proposals as PENDING.
writes: tm2mst.prod_speed_suggestion (PENDING); targets change only when PPIC accepts.

name: Preventive Plan Engine
purpose: Works out when each preventive plan is next due and opens the Draft preventive orders on time.
inputs: A Preventive Plan: time interval, meter interval or both, floating or fixed schedule, lead days.
The latest meter value of the asset (hours, km or count), for meter-based plans.
outputs: The date or meter value when the plan falls due next.
A preventive order with the plan checklist and spare parts copied in, never two open orders for one plan.
steps: Floating plans count from the last Closed order; fixed plans keep the calendar and skip missed dates.
A plan is due when the next due date is within its lead days, or the meter has reached the interval, whichever comes first.
generateDue (scheduled daily) opens a Draft order for every due plan that has no open order yet; the head of maintenance confirms it.
Closing the order moves the plan to its next due date.

name: Maintenance Order Lifecycle
purpose: Moves a Maintenance Order (PMO, BMO, IMO) from Draft to Closed and keeps the machine status and downtime log true.
inputs: The order with its checklist, spare parts and labor lines.
The head of maintenance decides (Confirm, Close, Cancel); technicians work (Start, Hold, Done).
outputs: PMO-, BMO- or IMO-yymm-nnnn, born at Confirm.
One downtime row for a machine asset that must stop, opened at Start and closed at Done.
Spare parts, labor at the standard rate and vendor service, final at Close.
steps: Draft can be edited freely; Confirm gives the number and puts the order in the technician list (Scheduled).
Start opens the downtime and sets the machine to Maintenance (planned) or Breakdown; assets that are not machines have no downtime.
Done is refused while a required checklist task has no result; it closes the downtime and sets the machine Ready.
Close fixes the cost and tells the plan to move to its next due date. Cancel needs a reason and closes any open downtime.

name: Maintenance Request Engine
purpose: Turns a problem report into a Breakdown Maintenance Order, and suggests how urgent it is.
inputs: Asset, kind (Breakdown, Corrective, Safety), whether the asset is stopped, and the symptom.
A machine breakdown reported on the shop floor in Work Order entry.
outputs: Suggested P1 to P3; the reporter may overrule it.
A Draft BMO when the head of maintenance accepts; a Confirmed BMO at once for P1.
steps: Safety is P1; a stopped machine of criticality A or B is P1; another stopped asset is P2; a critical asset that still runs is P2; the rest is P3.
P1 does not wait: the request is accepted and its BMO is confirmed so it shows in My Work immediately.
Other requests wait for the head of maintenance: Accept makes a Draft BMO, Reject needs a reason.
A shop floor breakdown creates one request per event; a machine without a Maintenance asset is skipped and the production report is never blocked.

name: Maintenance Spare Part Supply
purpose: Shows spare part stock on an order, issues the parts from the warehouse, and drafts a purchase requisition for what is short.
inputs: A Confirmed order in progress with spare part lines (planned and used quantity).
outputs: An ordinary raw material Stock Out per warehouse, posted through Inventory, so the stock card follows.
One Draft purchase requisition with the parts that stock cannot cover.
steps: On hand = usable stock of the material over all locations (Inventory view).
Issue takes each part from the locations with most stock; a part the stock cannot cover is skipped and reported, never half-issued.
Inventory is never written directly: the document is saved and posted by the Inventory services, which also refuse closed periods and negative stock.
Create PR needs a cost account for each short part (material category or item COGS account) and requests each line once.
used: Maintenance Order (Issue Parts, Create PR, In Stock column)

name: Maintenance KPI
purpose: Computes the Dashboard and report figures: availability, MTBF, MTTR, PM compliance, planned work, backlog, downtime and cost.
inputs: From and to dates, and optionally one machine.
outputs: Each figure, or nothing when it cannot be calculated; it is never shown as 0 for missing data.
What needs action today: machines down, open requests, overdue preventive orders, orders in progress or waiting for parts, critical parts below minimum.
steps: OEE, availability and MTBF / MTTR per machine come from the Production engine (MachineOeeService); Maintenance only adds up the machines.
MTBF = (machines x period hours - repair hours) / breakdowns; MTTR = repair hours / breakdowns.
PM compliance and planned work come from the orders; backlog = estimated hours of open orders / technician hours per week.
Targets are Constants (MNT_TARGET_*); the lamp compares each figure with its target.

name: Maintenance Machine Hold (Scheduling)
purpose: Tells Scheduling when a machine belongs to Maintenance, so production is never planned into those hours.
inputs: A time window and optionally the machines to look at.
outputs: Machine, start, end and order for every Confirmed order that must stop the machine.
steps: Counts orders that are Confirmed, not Done, Closed or Cancelled, need the machine stopped, and sit on an asset linked to the machine.
The window runs from the actual (or planned) start to the planned end, or start plus the estimate, or 60 minutes when neither is known.
Backward scheduling skips the window; a manual move into it is refused; the Scheduling Board draws it as MTN.

name: Paper Price Engine
purpose: Suggests the purchase price of paper per supplier: price per ream (standard size or cut from a roll), reams from a roll, price per purchase unit.
inputs: Raw material with grammage, size in cm and purchase unit.
Supplier of the PR suggestion or of the PO.
Document date; the price row in force on that date is used.
outputs: Price per purchase unit (RIM, LBR or KG) excluding PPN; empty when data is missing.
Reams from one roll of a given weight.
steps: Finds the active Supplier Paper Price row whose effective date is on or before the document date and whose paper kind appears in the material name; a matching grammage wins over an empty one.
Ream weight (kg) = length (m) x width (m) x grammage / 2.
Ream price = price per kg x ream weight / divisor; cut from a roll the price per kg is roll price (per kg, ton / 1000) + cut cost.
Divisor = 1 + PPN / 100 when the price includes PPN, otherwise 1; PPN is the Tax Rate screen rate in force on the document date (10% before 01-Apr-2022, 11% after).
LBR price = ream price / 500; KG price = roll price per kg / divisor.

name: Purchase Quotation Matcher
purpose: Matches the text of a supplier quotation file to the supplier master and to the requisition lines.
inputs: Supplier name as written in the file.
The lines of the requisition the quotation answers.
outputs: The requisition line or Material Master item and a percentage.
steps: Score = average of shared words (sizes and grammage count) and letter similarity.
First tries the requisition lines, then the Material Master.
A score below "sure" is marked yellow: the officer must choose.

entries.note: Builds or refreshes the register of one month; paid or filed rows are not changed.
Journal for the tax payment to the bank.
Records the filing reference.
Corporate income tax provision on the profit so far this year; only the difference is posted.
Register against ledger against source, for the status panel.

name: Tax Engine
purpose: Builds the monthly tax register (VAT, income tax 21 and 23), posts payments and reconciles with the ledger.
inputs: One register row to pay or file.
Payment date, state payment number and the bank account.
Who runs it and whether the data is live or dummy.
outputs: Per tax: base, tax, due dates, status.
Differences between register, ledger and source.
steps: Classify, calculate, post, reconcile, then pay and file.
All rates and due dates are read from the tax scheme table, so they change without code.
VAT payment nets output against input.

entries.note: May be repeated while the run is Draft or Calculated.
HR checks all employees or a random sample.
Locks attendance; refused while a payslip still has an anomaly.
Closes the period and opens the next one as an empty Draft.

name: Payroll Engine
purpose: Calculates the payslips of a period from attendance and takes the run through verification, payment and closing.
inputs: The payroll run being moved to its next status.
outputs: Draft, Calculated, Verified, Confirmed, Paid, Closed.
One per employee with its components.
An employee without an active salary rate stays visible and blocks Confirm.
steps: Loads the rule matrix (status, penalty, overtime) once per run.
Reads the daily attendance status of every employee in the period.
Builds each payslip: salary components, overtime per hour, deductions.
Verification, then Confirm locks attendance; Paid and Closed are status records.

name: Assistant Engine (offline)
purpose: Answers a question typed by the user without sending anything outside the company.
inputs: A help topic, for the "How to use" button.
outputs: A number, a help text, a screen to open, or "I do not know".
steps: Tries in order: a registered number whose phrase matches, help when the question has a question word, a screen, help without a question word, the local language model choosing among the closest candidates, then "I do not know".
Numbers come only from registered metric classes; the language model never calculates.
Help text is quoted from the help tables, never composed.

entries.note: One planning run. Writes a Draft only; the confirmed and locked part of the schedule is never touched.

name: PPIC Auto-Planner
purpose: Prepares a Draft plan for every open Work Order: gates, estimates, schedule and the list of what needs a person. Nothing becomes the real schedule until the officer confirms.
inputs: DAILY, SHIFT, EVENT (new Work Order, officer priority, drag) or MANUAL.
ENGINE or the officer who started it.
The moment to plan from (default: now).
outputs: One Draft run with the number of operations planned and the number that need attention.
Machine, start, finish, setup and gate of each operation, saved as Draft on the operation.
Late risk, material waiting, tooling blocked, no machine, overload.
steps: Refreshes Work Orders that have no process ids yet and re-reads the material and tooling gates.
Loads open operations outside the confirmed lock, the work calendar, holidays, wait rules and machine changeover values.
Hands the facts to the Schedule Solver, which ranks the jobs and places them on machines.
Discards the previous Draft, writes the new one and the exception list, and logs the run.
used: scheduler: ppic:auto-plan (nightly and at shift start)

name: Schedule Solver (finite capacity)
purpose: Pure calculation: ranks the jobs and places each operation on the machine that finishes it earliest, with setup, wait and calendar included.
inputs: Work Orders with their operations, candidate machines, rates, gates and fixed (running or locked) placements.
The work calendar: shifts per machine, holidays.
outputs: Machine, setup start, run start and finish per operation.
Late risk, blocked, waiting and no-machine operations with a reason.
steps: Ranks the Work Orders: Hot job first, then Critical Ratio below one, then due date; inside the similar-urgency window the setup-aware score decides.
Places the operations of a Work Order in routing order: each starts after the previous one finishes plus its wait.
For each operation picks the eligible machine with the earliest finish including setup, then lower load, then preference rank.
Same die (mall): jobs on one die inside the due tolerance are put one after the other, and a machine that already has the die is preferred when it finishes within the slack and the due date holds.
Machines are compared by clock time, not by work minutes of their own calendars.
A job confirmed and locked on a machine that is down is proposed on another machine in the Draft, with the reason; the officer decides at Confirm.
Fixed placements (running, locked) are never moved; blocked operations are listed, not placed.
reads: Nothing: it works on the facts it is given.

name: Setup Time Engine
purpose: Setup minutes and extra waste between two jobs on a machine: base setup plus every change (colour, ink type, substrate, size, plate, die) plus tool mounting.
inputs: Facts of the job before and the job after on the machine (colours, ink type, gsm, sheet size, plate, die).
Minutes and waste per kind of change; machine rows override the start values.
outputs: Total setup minutes and extra waste sheets.
The list of changes that produced them, for display.
steps: Starts from the base setup minutes of the machine (or the constant).
Adds one item for every difference between the two jobs, using the changeover table.
Adds the tool mounting minutes of the next job (first run or repeat run) from the tooling master.
When both jobs carry their real inks, a wash from light to dark inks is shortened by an assumed factor (PPIC_COLOR_ORDER_FACTOR).

name: Readiness Gates
purpose: Marks every operation Ready, Waiting (with a date) or Blocked (with a reason) for material, tooling and artwork.
inputs: The process of the operation (tooling needs a die or plates).
outputs: Ready, Waiting or Blocked per gate, with the note and the date material is ready.
steps: Material: reads the Material Planning result for the Work Order (stock, booking, incoming purchases); short material becomes Waiting with the incoming date, or Blocked when nothing is coming.
Tooling: looks up the plate set or die by dieline reference; Ready or In use passes, Not made, In making or Needs repair blocks; not registered passes with a note.
Writes the gates and the note on each operation.

name: Work Order Enrichment
purpose: Completes a new Work Order with what scheduling must know: process ids, the machines that can run each step, target per hour, waste, spoilage and setup.
inputs: A Work Order created from Product Development data.
outputs: Process id, quantity in and good out, target, setup minutes, candidate machines with eligibility and the reason when not eligible.
Sheet size, ups per sheet, board weight, colours, dieline reference, customer tier.
steps: Reads layout, board, colours, dieline and the customer tier from Product Development and the customer master.
Matches each operation to its process and checks every machine of that process against sheet size, board weight, colours and certification.
Takes the target per hour from the machine and process rates and estimates setup from the changeover table.
Flows quantities back from the last step: each step asks for what it needs including its waste and spoilage.

entries.note: Writes the real start and finish, sets Confirmed and locks the first N running shifts.

name: Plan Confirm and Change
purpose: The officer side of the plan: Confirm makes the Draft the real schedule and locks the next shifts; priority and drag changes go into a new Draft with their impact shown first.
outputs: Number of operations confirmed and locked.
steps: Only a Draft can be confirmed.
Copies the draft machine and times to the real columns, marks the operations Confirmed and Assigned.
Locks operations that start inside the next N running shifts (N = PPIC_LOCK_SHIFTS).
Writes the decision log.
used: Production Scheduling (Confirm plan, Hot job, Move up, Gantt drag)

name: Operator Timer
purpose: Play, Pause and Stop of the SETUP and PRODUCTION timers at the machine, and SAVE RESULT: records real setup, run and pause time and the good / bad quantities of each job, with a log row for every action.
inputs: The job in the confirmed queue of the crew machine and process.
Which timer (setup or production) and what to do: play, pause or stop.
Quantities of SAVE RESULT, added to what is already saved.
outputs: One row per segment: setup, run or pause.
Good quantity and bad (reject) lines in the production output tables.
One row per action: when, who, from which host, and the value before and after.
steps: One timer runs per machine at a time; Play on one timer pauses the other.
Pause closes the segment and opens a pause; Play continues that timer.
Stop locks that timer; Stop of production adds the setup minutes to the operation and finishes it.
SAVE RESULT adds good and bad to the saved quantities; progress = good / target qty, yield = good / (good + bad).

entries.note: Puts the old value back and freezes it so the engine leaves it alone.

name: Learning Engine (changeover)
purpose: Corrects the Assumed changeover minutes from the setup times operators really needed, in small logged steps that can be put back.
inputs: The logged change to put back.
outputs: Machine, kind of change, old and new minutes and the number of jobs.
One decision row per change (event LEARN or LEARN_REVERT).
steps: Takes the setup minutes of finished jobs per machine and kind of change from the time log.
Needs at least the minimum number of jobs; the typical actual is the median of the last ones minus the base setup.
New value = old + blend x (typical - old), moved by at most the step limit; only Assumed or Learning values that are not frozen.
Learns only from jobs finished after the last adjustment.

entries.note: Status of every product found in the PDF folder (ready or the reason it is skipped); writes nothing.
Dummy sets now in the database by the furthest document each reached, from Inquiry to a planned WO operation.
Builds the sets up to the quota of each level; products beyond the quota are noted, not built.
Removes everything this engine made: PDF Master Cards and, per card, the Inquiry chain down to WO, product, layout and files.

name: Master Card Dummy Engine (PDF to leveled dummy data)
purpose: Turns the new Master Card PDFs in docs/attachments/mastercard into leveled dummy data (Inquiry, Pro-Dev, Pro-Cost, Quotation WIN, Customer Order Confirmed), always with dieline, artwork and flat size. Dummy databases (ddt*) only; products already present are skipped, never overwritten.
inputs: Folder with the Master Card PDFs (default docs/attachments/mastercard).
Number of sets per level: inquiry, prodev, procost, co, product.
Order quantity of the sample Quotation and Customer Order.
Days from today for the Customer Order due date.
outputs: One row per product: design no., name, level reached, note (incomplete, skipped, over quota).
Collection cards and an Inquiry per product, plus layout, published costing, Quotation WIN and Confirmed CO as far as the level goes; data_origin DUMMY.
steps: Reads each PDF (MasterCardPdfReader) and groups the cards of one product by design number or card code.
Refuses to run unless the master, sales and production connections point to ddt* databases.
Checks the dummy requirements: artwork, P x L x T size, knife (flat size) and material; otherwise the product is reported as incomplete.
Level Inquiry: Collection cards with source file and artwork, customer ensured, Inquiry confirmed by Sales through InquiryWriter.
Level Pro-Dev: the layout canvas is built from the card (print size, knife layout, UP, press from the card text); BOP and BOM come from SpecEngine.
Level Pro-Cost and CO: costing is calculated and published, the Quotation is set to WIN and the Customer Order is created, approved and Confirmed.
Level product is a branch: the card becomes a Master Product directly, without Pro-Dev, Pro-Cost or Customer Order.
